facts.text: South Glastonbury hosted the Church Universal and Triumphant community during the 1980s and early 1990s, shaping its unique cultural landscape.
Nelson Story's 1866 herd of 600 Longhorn cattle drove from Texas into Shields Valley, supplying early ranches despite regional conflicts.
The Northern Pacific Railroad completed a spur from Livingston to Yellowstone National Park in 1902, linking South Glastonbury to the national park system.
South Glastonbury sits roughly 25 miles south of Livingston and 30 miles north of Yellowstone National Park, placing it between city and wilderness.
Fur trappers began arriving in the early 1820s, drawn by abundant beaver, establishing a presence that paved the way for later settlement.
Valley grasslands in South Glastonbury provided fertile land ideal for cattle ranching and grain farming, forming the backbone of early settlement activity.
